claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase fcc material.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has a suppressed orbital moment.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has a coercive field below 100 Oe.
Controlled thermal aging or rapid solidification can nucleate a Ti-rich secondary phase in the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The Ti-rich secondary phase could consist of TiFe or TiNi intermetallic precipitates.
The Ti-rich precipitates can form coherent or semi-coherent interfaces with the fcc matrix.
A sufficiently limited secondary-phase fraction can preserve overall fcc matrix continuity.
Coherent or semi-coherent precipitate interfaces induce local lattice strain.
The precipitate interfaces and associated strain modify the local electronic band structure.
Strain-induced symmetry breaking lifts d-orbital degeneracy and enhances orbital angular momentum.
The strain-induced orbital-moment enhancement counteracts the orbital-moment suppression of the single-phase fcc alloy.
Ti-rich secondary-phase precipitates act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Domain-wall pinning by the secondary phase increases coercivity.
The modified dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercive field exceeding 100 Oe.
The modified alloy will retain a Curie temperature significantly above room temperature.
The secondary phase will remain magnetically ordered or structurally stable at temperatures up to approximately 300–400 K.
The dual-phase alloy will show distinct pinning behavior in magnetic hysteresis loops that is absent from the single-phase baseline.

The proposed behavior requires the secondary-phase fraction to remain below a percolation threshold that would disrupt fcc matrix continuity or cause transformation to a nonmagnetic or low-Curie-temperature structure.
